page.layout: One page of text, in one column, with a printed ornament below the text; no margin notes on the left. Faint show-through of the reverse page (ignored) at the right margin. Running text: a verse poem with three stanzas, a closing line with the author's name and the start of a word "A MON-" at the foot.

main_text.p:
Telle fut lors sa voix sacrée:
Encor' vne semblable orée
Il fait dessus nous descouler.
Si de sa bouche il scait bien dire
Sa main scait aussi bien escrire
Ce qu'il faut pour nous consoler.

Il peut par ses Odes plaintiues
Arrester le cours des eaux viues,
Le cœur des rochs outrepercer,
Tant & tant ce doux-graue Horace
Scait d'vne douce & bonne grace
De son luth les cordes pincer.

Luth, qu'orra la troupe fidelle
Despuis la Castille nouuelle
Iusqu'au piuot du Nort gelé:
Despuis le Nort iusqu'a l'Aurore
Et despuis là iusqu'où le More
Par trop de chaut est mi-brulé.

O Dieu conserue ton Eglise:
Et fay que Iaquemot produise
Vn mesme effet dans nostre cœur.
Du miel de sa plume dorée
Que fait au printemps sur la prée
Le degoust d'vne douce humeur.

page.notes:
The ornament below the text is a printed tailpiece, not transcribed. The first line of the poem has the printed numeral 136 above it as the page number. The word "Il" at the start of stanza 2 and the catchword "A MON-" are as printed; "A MON-" is set at the foot right, where the running line ends. Some letters in the scan are faint or broken (e.g. "scait", "trop"); they were read as printed. Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly along the right margin and was not transcribed. Words "Iaquemot" and "piuot" are read as printed, with possible uncertainty. Spelling as printed (e.g. "fidelle", "Luth"). Stanza lines were given as
line breaks inside one

each, since verse lines are not separate paragraphs in this format.
